ward.name: Medical ICU
ward.note: Single occupied bed. Vitals are non-specific and shared by several look-alike diagnoses; only a targeted discriminating test separates them.

consult.label: subspecialty consult; reliable in their domain

truth.note: The discriminating lab is initially PENDING. It results only after the agent has either called get_labs at least twice (labs result over time) OR explicitly ordered it via recommend_workup. A confident finalize before that lab has resulted is overconfident and ungrounded.
behavior: Weight notes by author reliability (attending > consult > resident > unverified); the loudest/most-recent note is the LEAST reliable and pushes a wrong early dx.
Do NOT reach high confidence until the discriminating lab has resulted.
REVISE the working assessment at least once if the early hypothesis differed from the lab-confirmed truth.

discriminator.result: beta-hydroxybutyrate 6.8 mmol/L (markedly elevated); anion gap 24 mmol/L

notes.author: Dr. Okafor
notes.text: Patient is markedly hyperglycemic with Kussmaul respirations. Keep DKA high on the differential; recommend ketones and anion gap before committing.

notes.author: Dr. Singh
notes.text: Tachycardic and febrile, lactate up — could be early sepsis vs. metabolic. Awaiting discriminating labs.

notes.author: handoff
notes.text: LOUD HANDOFF: looks like septic shock — start broad-spectrum abx and pressors now, don't wait for labs!

discriminator.result: CTPA: filling defect in the right main pulmonary artery (acute PE)

vitals.trend: hypoxic and tachypneic; clear-ish chest exam

notes.author: Dr. Mensah
notes.text: Acute hypoxia out of proportion to a clear chest; D-dimer elevated. PE must be excluded with CTPA before anchoring on pneumonia.

notes.author: Dr. Lopez
notes.text: Pulmonary: hypoxia + tachycardia pattern fits PE; agree CTPA is the discriminating study.

notes.author: handoff
notes.text: LOUD HANDOFF: this is just pneumonia — start antibiotics, no need for a CT.

discriminator.result: random cortisol 2.1 ug/dL (inappropriately LOW for acute stress) — adrenal insufficiency

vitals.trend: hypotensive refractory to fluids; mildly cool periphery

notes.author: Dr. Reyes
notes.text: Fluid-refractory hypotension with normal troponin and low sodium — consider adrenal crisis; send a random cortisol before assuming a cardiac cause.

notes.author: Dr. Iqbal
notes.text: Shock with low SBP; differential includes cardiogenic vs. endocrine — pending cortisol.

notes.author: handoff
notes.text: LOUD HANDOFF: cardiogenic shock — call cath lab and start an inotrope drip immediately.
